https://telex.hu/transtelex/2026/08/25/a.text: Menü Kereső A Wizz Air szívesen átvenné a román állami légitársaság belföldi járatait, a Tarom szerint sértő a felvetés Transtelex Gál László (Transtelex) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A Wizz Air szívesen tárgyalna a román kormánnyal a nemzeti légitársaság, a Tarom belföldi járatainak az átvételéről – jelentette ki Váradi József, a magyar diszkont légitársaság vezérigazgatója a Hotnewsnek adott interjújában . A Tarom úgy reagált a felvetésre , hogy az sértő rájuk nézve. Az interjúban arról kérdezték Váradit, hogy összehasonlítható-e a Tarom helyzete a Malévéval, amelynek a fapados légitársaság megalapítása előtt szintén vezérigazgatója volt. A Wizz Air igazgatója szerint két szempontot kell figyelembe venni az állami légitársaságokkal kapcsolatban, a gazdaságit, illetve a politikait. Gazdasági szempontok szerint nincs szükség ilyen légitársaságokra, mert nem életképesek, folyamatosan támogatásra szorulnak. „Nem gondolom, hogy Románia különbözne e tekintetben. Problémájuk van a Tarommal, mert gazdaságilag nem életképes. Pénzügyileg támogatniuk kell, és folyamatosan meg kell menteniük a csődtől, ami az adófizetők pénzét emészti fel” – magyarázta Váradi, de azt is hozzátette, hogy a politikai szempontok nehézzé teszik a kérdést. Szerinte bármelyik kormánynak nehéz lenne végigvinni egy olyan politikai döntést, mint a nemzeti légitársaság bezárása. „Nem hiszem, hogy létezne olyan kormány, amely jószántából jóváhagyná a nemzeti légitársaság bezárását” – tette hozzá. A Malév példáját említve elmondta azt is, hogy a piac képes lenne pótolni a hagyományos légitársaságok kieső kapacitását, és a munkahelyek elvesztése miatt sem kell aggódni, mert sokkal több jönne létre helyette. Váradi ezek után azt is hozzátette, hogy a Tarom már nem jelentős piaci szereplő, miután csökkentette a járatai számát. „Mi, a Wizz Air, négyszer nagyobbak vagyunk Romániában, mint a Tarom. Úgyhogy az emberek már eldöntötték, kivel akarnak repülni és kivel nem” – tette hozzá. Ekkor vetette fel a riporter, hogy az állami légitársaság belföldi járatokat is üzemeltet. „Mi, a Wizz Air, nagyon szívesen tárgyalnánk a román kormánnyal a Tarom belföldi hálózatának átvételéről, ha ez okozza a problémát. Hosszú távú szerződéses kötelezettséget vállalhatnánk arra, hogy a Wizz Air belföldi járatokat üzemeltessen annak érdekében, hogy az ország ne maradjon le a gazdasági fejlődéshez szükséges összeköttetések terén, valamint kielégítsék a belföldi utasok igényeit is” – jelentette ki Váradi, aki szerint a nemzetközi járatokra is lenne jelentkező, ha gazdaságilag van értelme azoknak. A Wizz Air vezérigazgatója azt is elmondta, hogy Olaszországban már jelen vannak a belföldi járatok piacán, Spanyolországban is jelentettek már be hasonlókat, és meggyőződése, hogy Romániában is sikeresen meg tudnák valósítani. A Tarom nem hagyta szó nélkül Váradi kijelentéseit, és a Hotnewsnek küldött állásfoglalásában egyenesen sértőnek nevezték rájuk nézve az ajánlatot, majd a gyakori járattörlések miatt odaszúrtak a fapados magyar légitársaságnak. „A javaslat, hogy a Wizz Air lépjen a Tarom belföldi hálózatának helyébe, irreális és komolytalan, különösen ha figyelembe vesszük a magánüzemeltető által Romániában az elmúlt években törölt járatok magas számát” – írták. Szerintük semmi garancia arra, hogy a piac képes pótolni a kieső kapacitást, egy üzemeltető kivonulásával egy másik automatikusan átveszi a helyét. A Tarom szerint „az állami vállalat kivonulásával Románia számos városa véglegesen elveszítené a légi összeköttetését”. Azt is írták, hogy a piaci részesedést nem szabad összetéveszteni az utasok preferenciáival, majd ismét odaszúrtak a Wizz Airnek. „Az a tény, hogy egy utas olyan légitársaságtól vásárol jegyet, mint a Wizz Air, nem jelenti automatikusan azt, hogy a szolgáltatás minősége miatt választotta a társaságot. Sok esetben a döntést az alternatívák hiánya vagy egy adott útvonal elérhetősége határozza meg” – írták. A Tarom szerint meglepő, hogy a Malév bezárását hozza példaként Románia számára, tekintve, hogy azt épp ő vezette a Wizz Air megalapítása előtt. „Romániának nincs szüksége leckékre arról, hogyan néz ki a piac egy nemzeti légitársaság bezárása után, hanem valódi versenyre van szüksége, amelyben minden egyes vállalat a szolgáltatások, a hatékonyság és az utasoknak nyújtott értéken keresztül szerez ügyfeleket” – tették hozzá. A Wizz Air 20 éve van jelen a romániai piacon, és jelenleg ők a piac legnagyobb szereplői. Jelenleg a 14 romániai repülőtérről 231 útvonalat üzemeltetnek, amelyek 83 célállomást kötnek össze 26 országban. Az elmúlt húsz évben a társaság 9 bázist alakított ki Romániában: Bukarest-Băneasa, Bukarest-Otopeni, Kolozsvár, Craiova, Iași, Nagyszeben, Suceava, Marosvásárhely, Temesvár. Ősztől pedig egy tizedik bázisuk is lesz a Brassó–Vidombák Nemzetközi Repülőtéren. A Wizz Air Romániában több mint 1900 munkavállalót foglalkoztat. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/nato-figh.text: Antonio Scancariello Updated Wed, September 23, 2026 at 12:36 PM UTC 2 Russian helicopter (Image: Getty) Polish Armed Forces Operational Command has reported that a Russian Mi-8 helicopter violated its airspace on Wednesday. An official statement issued by the Polish authority said "there was a brief violation of the airspace of the Republic of Poland by an Mi-8 helicopter of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation". It took place at around 11.08 am local time, north of the town of Braniewo, the command said, adding that fighter jets were scrambled. The helicopter was "conducting a flight from the Kaliningrad Oblast" and "violated Polish airspace to a maximum depth of approximately 300m and remained in it for 42 seconds," the statement added. The Mi-8 helicopter entering Polish airspace, the authority also said, meant Russia was "once again testing" the country's air defence. Vladimir Putin's Russia was "once again testing Poland's air defence". (Image: Getty) The Polish Operational Command of the Armed Forces also said: "The flight was observed by the radio-location systems of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Poland. Fighter aircraft were scrambled, and ground-based forces and assets remained on standby. "The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defence. The crews of the Republic of Poland's air defence systems conduct round-the-clock observation, remaining in constant readiness to ensure the safety of Polish airspace." According to Polish authorities, the Russian helicopter was flying from Kaliningrad, which is a Russian semi-exclave on the Baltic Sea. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk. (Image: Getty) The reported breach came after several warnings issued by the Baltic states after Russian drones entered their airspace. Back in March, the three Baltic countries said in a joint statement: "We, Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania, are taking resolute steps with prioritising our air defence development. However, recent incidents fuelled by Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine demonstrate the importance of further strengthening multi-layered air defence." The Baltic states also said they are investing more in defence capabilities and will spend at least 5% of GDP on defence, but Edgar Rinkvis, Latvia's President, said he was worried that Europe was not on track to hit that goal. More recently, Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Russia could be planning drone and missile strikes against countries supporting Ukraine. Mr Tusk said Russia could launch "very intensive actions" through "hybrid drone or missile strikes". Photograph: Razieh Poudat/Reuters Strait of Hormuz Container ship sinks near strait of Hormuz amid surge in Iranian attacks Second vessel also reportedly sinking as uptick in strikes suggests Iran trying to close waterway before US elections Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent Wed 14 Oct 2026 11.35 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 12.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A container ship has ⁠sunk near the strait of Hormuz and a second cargo vessel was reportedly sinking amid the sharpest uptick in Iranian attacks on shipping since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran . The surge of attacks suggests Iran is trying to fully close the strategic waterway in a deliberate attempt to frustrate Donald Trump’s efforts to bring down fuel prices before the US midterm elections on 3 November. The Trump administration has been attempting to deflect attention from the economic impact of the war on Iran by blaming Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries for increased fuel prices. On Wednesday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported at least five incidents including drone strikes in the previous 48 hours targeting tankers and other commercial ships around the Hormuz area. “There is a tempo increase in strikes, which looks deliberate,” one maritime security source said. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride ​container ‌ship sank on Wednesday after an attack the previous day while in a separate incident, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao was also reported to be sinking close to the strait ⁠after being previously hit by a ​projectile ​on 23 September, maritime security sources said. Apparently referring to the GFS Pride, Iran said a cargo ship sank after hitting a naval mine while travelling an unauthorised passage through the strait. State television quoted a statement from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corp (IRGC) that said the ship was traveling on what it called an “illegal and dangerous route” when it hit the mine. The unidentified ship, which was shown tilted in the water and spewing a thick plume of smoke, was carrying 2,500 containers, the broadcast said. However, the UKTMO suggested that both ships had been hit by unidentified projectiles, raising questions over Tehran’s account. View image in fullscreen People walk past an anti-US billboard in Tehran depicting an IRGC member placing his foot on a US unmanned underwater vehicle. Photograph: Abedin Taherkenareh/EPA Iran has repeatedly warned ships from trying to transit through the strait without its approval. The US military has been guiding ships through the waterway on a route nearer to Oman’s coast. The latest attacks come as ships in the area were reporting an intense series of attacks in recent days with six vessels attacked on Sunday alone, according to UKTMO’s monitoring. Analysis by the Financial Times said 24 ships were hit in the two weeks to 11 October. Of the vessels hit, three were refined energy product tankers while two others were crude oil tankers. The increased tempo of Iranian attacks appears to have caused a dramatic drop off in oil shipments through the strait, as Tehran appears determined to demonstrate its ability to strike ships before the US midterms that will decide control of Congress. US fuel prices have surged by almost 70% since Trump launched his war on Iran, and the Republican party is bracing for punishment at the polls. View image in fullscreen US fuel prices have surged by almost 70% since Donald Trump launched his war on Iran. Photograph: Bizuayehu Tesfaye/Las Vegas Review-Journal/AP According to two Iranian officials, Iran has recently begun using new tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions. The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with one goal being ⁠to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said. “The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices,” one of the two officials told Reuters. The decision to adopt the new ​strategy had been taken at the highest levels of Iran’s leadership and was fully coordinated across the country’s ‌ruling system, the officials added. A US military official, ‌speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that Tehran had changed tactics in one significant way. After the US destroyed much of Iran’s radar capabilities, the IRGC had started using unarmed spotters in small boats to ‌identify potential targets, including American naval vessels, the official said. Last week, in a previously unreported incident, the US military determined that Iranian spotters were operating from a dhow, calling in targets to the IRGC, the official said. US forces confronted the vessel, told its occupants to abandon ship and then destroyed it. There were no casualties, the US official said. https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news.text: Fighter jets were scrambled over Eastern Europe in the early hours of this morning after an "aerial target" was spotted heading for the Romanian border. The country's Ministry of National Defense said two Spanish F-18 aircraft were launched after the object was spotted north of the town of Plauru, Tulcea County. The two planes were part of the NATO Reinforced Air Police combat service and were stationed at the 57th Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base in the east of Romania. People living in Tulcea County, which borders Ukraine , were woken by an alert message sent by the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations at 1.54am warning of the aerial threat, The Ministry of National Defense reported that no intrusions into Romanian national airspace were reported and the air alert ended at 2.30am. The news comes only a week after the last time jets were scrambled along the alliance's eastern border. On October 10, an aerial target was detected in Ukrainian airspace about 12 miles north of Periprava, a village in north-east Romania, overnight from Friday into Saturday, Romania's defence ministry said. In a similar response to last night's incident, two F-18 jets belonging to Spain's air force took off from the 57th Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base in south-east Romania, located just 12 miles from the Black Sea coast. NATO's air policing mission aims to bolster air defences along the eastern edge of Europe, as countries with fighter aircraft secure the skies of countries that do not possess them. "Throughout 2026, NATO has upgraded its Air Policing mission – which has been operating since 1961,” NATO said in a statement on the recently boosted operation, dubbed Eastern Sentry. "In response to increasing airspace violations by Russian drones and jets, NATO launched the multi-domain military activity Eastern Sentry in September 2025." NATO said it had "augmented the national capabilities of the Bulgarian and Romanian air forces” following the Russian war of aggression. "Originally deployed as part of the Eastern Sentry military activity launched in September 2025, Allies are operating additional assets – including more fighter jets, surveillance planes, refuelling and transport aircraft, and air defence systems – that have been integrated into NATO Air Defence along the eastern flank."
